title: Zyxel fixes zero-day exploited to hack nearly 1,000 network switches
content_md: Zyxel has patched a zero-day vulnerability in its GS1900 series network switches that hackers exploited to compromise nearly 1,000 devices worldwide and steal configuration files and credentials. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-107441, is an out-of-bounds write flaw in the switches' web management interface that allows an unauthenticated attacker with network access to execute operating system commands using specially crafted HTTP requests. The flaw affects ten GS1900 switch models, and Zyxel released security updates on October 22 and published a security advisory on November 3. However, the vulnerability was initially mistaken for an older flaw that Zyxel had already patched months before the attacks began. On June 16, 2026, Zyxel released security updates addressing CVE-2026-7273, a pre-authentication buffer overflow vulnerability affecting the same GS1900 switches. Starting around August 17, cybersecurity company GreyNoise observed a suspected Chinese-speaking threat actor tracked as Kapibala exploiting Zyxel switches, reporting that the attackers compromised 996 devices across 48 countries. The threat actors exploited the flaw to execute commands remotely before downloading a script that collected device configurations, hashed root credentials, and network information.
